papers.title: Funneled Bayesian Optimization for Design, Tuning and Control of Autonomous Systems
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization has become a fundamental global optimization algorithm in many problems where sample efficiency is of paramount importance. Recently, there has been proposed a large number of new applications in fields such as robotics, machine learning, experimental design, simulation, etc. In this paper, we focus on several problems that appear in robotics and autonomous systems: algorithm tuning, automatic control and intelligent design. All those problems can be mapped to global optimization problems. However, they become hard optimization problems. Bayesian optimization internally uses a probabilistic surrogate model (e.g.: Gaussian process) to learn from the process and reduce the number of samples required. In order to generalize to unknown functions in a black-box fashion, the common assumption is that the underlying function can be modeled with a stationary process. Nonstationary Gaussian process regression cannot generalize easily and it typically requires prior knowledge of the function. Some works have designed techniques to generalize Bayesian optimization to nonstationary functions in an indirect way, but using techniques originally designed for regression, where the objective is to improve the quality of the surrogate model everywhere. Instead optimization should focus on improving the surrogate model near the optimum. In this paper, we present a novel kernel function specially designed for Bayesian optimization, that allows nonstationary behavior of the surrogate model in an adaptive local region. In our experiments, we found that this new kernel results in an improved local search (exploitation), without penalizing the global search (exploration). We provide results in well-known benchmarks and real applications. The new method outperforms the state of the art in Bayesian optimization both in stationary and nonstationary problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了针对非平稳函数的贝叶斯优化方法，可转移至生物力学设计的替代模型优化中，但未涉及约束处理、不确定性量化或具体植入物设计验证。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address multi-objective or constraint handling, lacks explicit uncertainty quantification beyond standard GP, and provides no validation in biomechanics or implant design contexts.

summary_zh.motivation: 提高贝叶斯优化在非平稳函数上的采样效率。
summary_zh.method: 提出一种自适应局部非平稳核函数，专注于最优区域建模。
summary_zh.result: 新核在平稳和非平稳问题上均超越现有方法。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准基准测试和实际应用中验证。

summary_en.motivation: To improve sample efficiency of Bayesian optimization on nonstationary functions.
summary_en.method: Proposes a novel nonstationary kernel that adaptively focuses on the local region near the optimum.
summary_en.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art Bayesian optimization on both stationary and nonstationary problems.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on standard benchmark functions and real-world applications.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文是临床随机对照试验，比较手术入路对步态和肌力的影响，不涉及任何生物力学建模或植入物力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not include FEA, stress shielding quantification, micromotion analysis, or any implant-bone interface mechanics; it is purely a clinical outcome study.

summary_zh.motivation: 比较直接外侧入路和后外侧入路对全髋置换术后步态和肌力的影响。
summary_zh.method: 前瞻性随机对照试验，12个月随访评估步态和肌力。
summary_zh.result: 两种入路在步态和肌力恢复上无显著差异。
summary_zh.validation: 临床试验，包含患者招募和随访测量。

summary_en.motivation: To compare the effect of modified direct lateral versus posterior surgical approach on gait function and hip muscle strength after primary total hip arthroplasty.
summary_en.method: An explorative randomized controlled trial with 12-month follow-up assessing gait parameters and muscle strength.
summary_en.result: No significant differences in gait function or muscle strength were found between the two approaches.
summary_en.validation: Clinical trial with patient recruitment and standardized follow-up measurements.

papers.title: Humorous materials to enhance active learning
papers.abstract: The use of humour in teaching and learning can be contentious, with some authors suggesting that the efficacy of humorous materials is mediated by the culture of the student. Nevertheless, humour represents a potential vehicle for the introduction of active learning in a classroom setting, as judicious use of humour may lead to a more relaxed learning atmosphere and greater student engagement. This article describes how humour was used to good effect in creating a suite of online materials designed to enhance the academic English skills of international students. The materials, funded through a grant from the Office for Learning and Teaching and now openly accessible on the English for Uni website, were developed using an action research process. This involved an iterative process of designing, trialling and evaluating the resources to ensure that humour was used appropriately. In the final stages, Biggs’ Structure of the Observed Learning Outcome taxonomy was also used to evaluate student learning. The results show that the materials improved students’ understanding of the topics presented on the site and that the element of humour stimulated student interest in learning.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address FEA, surrogate modeling, optimization, uncertainty quantification, or any engineering or biomedical design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 探索幽默材料在提升国际学生学术英语技能中的作用。
summary_zh.method: 通过行动研究迭代设计、试用和评估在线幽默学习资源。
summary_zh.result: 幽默材料提高了学生对主题的理解并激发了学习兴趣。
summary_zh.validation: 使用Biggs的SOLO分类法评估学生学习成果。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate whether humorous materials can enhance active learning and engagement in academic English for international students.
summary_en.method: An action research approach was used to iteratively design, trial, and evaluate online resources incorporating humour.
summary_en.result: The humorous materials improved students' understanding of topics and stimulated their interest in learning.
summary_en.validation: Student learning was evaluated using Biggs' Structure of the Observed Learning Outcome (SOLO) taxonomy.

papers.title: Statistical Framework for Uncertainty Quantification in Computational Molecular Modeling
papers.abstract: As computational modeling, simulation, and predictions are becoming integral parts of biomedical pipelines, it behooves us to emphasize the reliability of the computational protocol. For any reported quantity of interest (QOI), one must also compute and report a measure of the uncertainty or error associated with the QOI. This is especially important in molecular modeling, since in most practical applications the inputs to the computational protocol are often noisy, incomplete, or low-resolution. Unfortunately, currently available modeling tools do not account for uncertainties and their effect on the final QOIs with sufficient rigor. We have developed a statistical framework that expresses the uncertainty of the QOI as the probability that the reported value deviates from the true value by more than some user-defined threshold. First, we provide a theoretical approach where this probability can be bounded using Azuma-Hoeffding like inequalities. Second, we approximate this probability empirically by sampling the space of uncertainties of the input and provide applications of our framework to bound uncertainties of several QOIs commonly used in molecular modeling. Finally, we also present several visualization techniques to effectively and quantitavely visualize the uncertainties: in the input, final QOIs, and also intermediate states.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文关注分子建模中的不确定性量化，而非生物力学有限元代理建模，方法框架可能具有参考价值但领域差异大。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on molecular modeling, not on FEA surrogate modeling for implant or biomechanics design; it lacks any application to solid mechanics or structural optimization.

summary_zh.motivation: 分子建模中缺乏对输入不确定性的严格量化。
summary_zh.method: 提出基于Azuma-Hoeffding不等式的概率界和输入空间采样的经验近似。
summary_zh.result: 实现了对分子建模中多个感兴趣量的不确定性边界估计。
summary_zh.validation: 通过理论推导和分子建模案例验证。

summary_en.motivation: To address the lack of rigorous uncertainty quantification in computational molecular modeling pipelines.
summary_en.method: Developed a statistical framework using Azuma-Hoeffding inequalities for theoretical bounds and empirical sampling for approximation.
summary_en.result: Demonstrated bounded uncertainties for several quantities of interest in molecular modeling.
summary_en.validation: Validated through theoretical proofs and application to molecular modeling examples.
